title: One partition, two choices
sub: During a partition, London can refuse to answer (CP) or answer with what it has (AP).

frames.caption: Your balance, 400, is stored on two replicas: New York and London. Each serves the ATMs on its side of the Atlantic.
You withdraw 200 in New York. NY records it and replicates to London over the cable. Both replicas agree.
The undersea cable is cut. The two replicas can no longer talk. Both are still running: this is a network partition.
You withdraw another 100 in New York. NY records it, but cannot tell London.
Someone with your card tries to withdraw 150 in London. A CP system's London replica knows it cannot confirm it has the latest balance, so it refuses: an error, not an answer.
The cable is repaired. London catches up from New York. Nothing needs reconciling, because London never acted on stale data. The price was that London was dark for the whole partition.

Someone tries to withdraw 150 in London. An AP system's London replica answers with what it has: balance 200, so the withdrawal is allowed. London stays open.

The cable is repaired, and the replicas disagree: NY says 100, London says 50. Neither is right. 450 was withdrawn from an account holding 400. The system must reconcile (merge the two histories) and the bank must deal with an overdraft. That is the price of staying available.
